Definition of done:
- `GET /v1/invoices` (any mix of `customer_id`, `subscription_id`, `status`, `limit`, `cursor`) now reads from a per-organization sorted index instead of copying and sorting every invoice in the store. It builds views only for the page, and looks up each customer directly. Output is unchanged: same order, fields, errors and cursors.
- Store and HTTP tests compare paging against the full list across orgs, filters and page sizes, and cover invoices created between pages, status changes, and a snapshot restore. Checked with `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...`, all passing.
- No exported names or signatures changed. `ListInvoices` keeps its behavior.

## Result

The fix is in `internal/store/billing.go`, `store.go`, `state.go` and `internal/api/invoices.go`. The old path copied every invoice in the store through a JSON clone, sorted them all, then loaded every customer and scanned that list for each invoice. The new path finds the start of the page by binary search and stops after one page of matches.

Timing, measured with a temporary test that I deleted afterwards: 60,000 invoices for Acme (about a quarter paid), 5,000 customers, and 30,000 invoices for another org. Worst case was about 7 ms (a `customer_id` filter that scans the whole list). Other requests took 0.1 to 5.6 ms. The 100 ms target has a wide margin.

- `internal/store/billing.go`: `InvoicePosition` and `InvoicePage` (new); `ListInvoices` now uses the index; `indexInvoice` keeps the index sorted on create; `cloneInvoice` removed because nothing uses it now.

What I checked:

- **Output fields and customer lookup:** `viewInvoice` (`internal/api/invoices.go:50`) looks the customer up with `s.store.Customer(orgID, id)`, which is org-scoped. That matches the old `findCustomer` over `Customers(orgID)`, and `newInvoiceView` builds the same fields.
